messages:
dan_acme: Hey team — after our account-to-account VPC migration yesterday (vpc-0a1b2c3d -> vpc-0f4e5d6c) our app cannot resolve service.api.acme.internal anymore, getting NXDOMAIN from app hosts. This started at ~09:12 UTC. Can you help?

alice_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a quick `dig` from one of the affected instances and the VPC id + account id? Also, did you change Route53/private zones during the migration?

dan_acme: Repro steps short: deploy app -> curl internal URL -> fails. From an app pod (k8s on EC2) I ran:```
$ dig +short service.api.acme.internal

# (empty) -> NXDOMAIN when resolv.conf uses `search acme.internal`
```
And full dig:```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> service.api.acme.internal
;; global options: +cmd
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 52345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
```

VPC: vpc-0f4e5d6c (account 987654321000). The private zone used to be in account 111122223333. We used RAM to share VPC association during migration.

bob_infra: Two quick suspicion buckets: 1) private hosted zone not actually associated to the new VPC (cross-account association via RAM didn't complete), or 2) Route53 Resolver rules / forwarders now taking precedence and forwarding to the wrong resolver (split-horizon mismatch).

charlie_sre: Also check the VPC DNS settings (enableDnsHostnames/enableDnsSupport) and DHCP options set — if those changed the instances might not be using AmazonProvidedDNS.

alice_support: Can you run these and paste outputs?```
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "acme.internal"
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZEXAMPLE123
aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id ZEXAMPLE123
aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=DomainName,Values=acme.internal
```
If cross-account: `aws ram get-resource-shares` and `aws ram get-resource-share-invitations` for the zone share.

dan_acme: Pasting trimmed outputs:```
$ aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZEXAMPLE123
{"HostedZone": {"Id": "/hostedzone/ZEXAMPLE123","Name": "acme.internal.","Config": {"PrivateZone": true}}}
$ aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id ZEXAMPLE123
{"VPCs": []}  # empty -> looks like no pending cross-account assoc
$ aws route53 list-vpc-associations-for-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id ZEXAMPLE123
{"VPCs": [{"VPCId": "vpc-0a1b2c3d","VPCRegion": "us-west-2","OwningAccount": "111122223333"}]}
```
So the zone is still associated to the old VPC (vpc-0a1b2c3d in account 1111...), not to the new vpc in account 9876...

bob_infra: That matches the NXDOMAIN. Private hosted zones only resolve for associated VPCs. The cross-account association via RAM won't magically move the association; you have to explicitly associate the hosted zone to the target VPC (or re-associate via the owning account). Two options: 1) owner account (1111...) runs `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` for the new VPC id and account, or 2) create a new private hosted zone in the target account and populate records (not ideal).

charlie_sre: Quick checklist: - confirm hosted zone owner is reachable/has permissions - confirm VPC association exists for target VPC - check resolver rules: if there's a FORWARD rule for `acme.internal` that points to an on-prem resolver that now blocks requests, that could also return NXDOMAIN. Run `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations` in the new VPC.

alice_support: Also check there isn't an overlapping public or different private zone with higher priority (same name) in the new account. Overlap can make lookups ambiguous.

dan_acme: I tried `dig @172.31.0.2 service.api.acme.internal` (the VPC resolver) and get NXDOMAIN as well. No forwarder configured intentionally.

bob_infra: Action plan: (1) I'll ping the owner account infra (111122223333) to request assoc for vpc-0f4e5d6c (account 987654321000). (2) Charlie, can you check resolver-rule associations from our side in account 9876? (3) Dan, don't make changes to hosted zone yet — we'll coordinate.

charlie_sre: Running on my side now: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0f4e5d6c` returns nothing relevant for domain `acme.internal` — so no forwarder in this VPC.

alice_support: I'm marking this P1 and creating internal case SUP-4582. Notifying eng-infra for cross-account assoc. If owner account needs us to accept a RAM share we'll coordinate. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy-2026-03-17-service-migration completed by dan_acme at 09:05 UTC — no errors reported during deploy.

dan_acme: Thanks. If the owner account needs me to raise a ticket there, let me know. Appreciate the quick triage. :pray:

bob_infra: I'll DM infra in the owner account and escalate to the zone owner. Expect follow-up in ~30min. For completeness, once assoc is created, test `dig` from an instance in vpc-0f4e5d6c and validate records. If still failing, we can check IAM permissions and policy on the hosted zone.

alice_support: Follow-up: SUP-4582 created, linked to this thread. Next update at 10:00 UTC or when assoc completed.
